footnotes: Morris Ketchum Jesup was an American banker and philanthropist, who supported scientific research and collected art. He was the third president of the American Museum of Natural History in New York, serving from 1881 until his death in 1908.

did_you_know: The swirling kusikos pattern was meant to confuse evil spirits and had a protective function.
description: This intricate, hand-woven textile was likely produced on a back-strap or upright loom. The binakol block pattern creates a strong optical effect, organized in vertical registers separated by broad, dark stripes with narrow, red accents. The central design is a variant of the whirlpool motif known as kusikos, in which alternating light and dark squares appear to spiral or recede.
